solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old college, as well as railway, drawing various fellows into partnership

parts.note: a poly was a polytechnic, a British college type abolished in 1992
as well as means and

explanation.surface: An old college and a railway company merge, bringing assorted staff into a new partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY (a former British polytechnic) is the old college; the definition reads cryptically as one woman taking several men into marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a marriage system where one woman has several husbands, so various men join her partnership.

clue.text: Topical broadcast gets across name of philosopher

indicators.note: gets across means the scrambled letters stretch round the name letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A topical broadcast gets a philosopher's name across to its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TOPICAL to PLATOIC; 'gets across' places N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Plato, the Greek thinker, so it describes a philosopher's ideas.

clue.text: Story about fine periods of sleep reflecting normal existence

indicators.note: about means the story letters go round the fine letter

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: reflecting means the sleep word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: naps are short periods of sleep

explanation.surface: A story about how good sleep reflects a normal life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' turns NAPS into SPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the length of a living thing's life, its usual existence from birth to death.

clue.text: Claim to see rising jazz queen turning up for one

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the name is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: Ella Fitzgerald was the First Lady of Song, queen of jazz

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means these letters go bottom to top

parts.note: for one means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A claim to have seen a jazz singer coming up the bill, appearing as one example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ELLA into ALLE; 'turning up' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something without proof is to make a claim.

clue.text: Duke up North tracks birds

parts.note: in northern English dialect a rake is a track or path up a hillside

explanation.surface: A duke follows tracks in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: In the north of England, a rake is a steep path or track; up North means in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: These are male ducks, so they are birds.

clue.text: Vigorous lad's not quite 18 Across

parts.note: a lad is a youth; the 's is a link

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the answer at 18 Across means satisfied, which is full

explanation.surface: A vigorous lad is not quite satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 Across is REPLETE, meaning FULL, which 'not quite' cuts to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being young in spirit implies energy and vigour.

clue.text: Fruit worker's success

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in a firm's men; the 's is a link
to make a go of something is to make a success of it

explanation.surface: A labourer's achievement is described, as if it were the fruit of his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with orange flesh, plainly a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Rule out first name misspelt in list of passengers

indicators.note: misspelt means the letters are written in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An official rules out a first name spelt wrongly in a passenger list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes R (rule) from FIRST NAME, and 'misspelt' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's or plane's manifest is the official register of its cargo and passengers.

clue.text: Rovers on form regularly will gain advantage over Sweden

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

parts.note: AD is short for advantage, the tennis score
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A football club called Rovers, in form, will regularly beat Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes N, O, M from ON FORM. Rovers looks like a football team; it means wanderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandering peoples with no fixed home are rovers.

clue.text: 'Dropsy' found in dictionary condensed by English graduate

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary condensed to initials is OED
an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: The word dropsy is found in a shortened dictionary edited by an English graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for swelling caused by fluid in body tissues, the modern medical term.

clue.text: Lucerne Academy has pursued Garnett twice

indicators.note: the Garnett pieces come after, chasing the Academy letter
twice asks for the name to be written two times in a row

parts.note: Alf Garnett was the bigoted lead of the British sitcom Till Death Us Do Part

explanation.surface: Someone at an academy in the Swiss city of Lucerne has been chasing a man named Garnett twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucerne looks like the Swiss city, but it is the plant. ALF GARNETT was a famous British TV bigot of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for the fodder plant called by its other name in America.

clue.text: Pool said to revive seabird

indicators.note: said signals that the word for pool is spoken, giving the sound only

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money shared by players
to wake is to revive or bring round

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have revived a pool, perhaps restarting a betting fund.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gull of cliffs and open ocean, named for its call, so a seabird.

clue.text: Young crabs?

parts.note: children are informally called by a word that also names claws, which crabs have; so small kids who complain, or pincers

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'crabs' as grumblers: young grumblers are children, informally called by this word, which also means the claws of crabs.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for small children, and also a word for the pincers that crabs wield.

clue.text: Flower on the house is falling back by start of autumn

parts.note: something on the house is given free of charge

indicators.note: falling back means the little word is read backwards
start of means only the opening letter of autumn is used

explanation.surface: A free flower in the garden of a house is wilting as autumn begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling back' turns IS into SI; 'start of' takes the A of autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant bulb plant from southern Africa with trumpet-shaped blooms grown as a cut flower.

clue.text: One that's offended by rambling naturist: 'Gaol would be well done'

parts.note: a con is a convict, someone who has committed an offence

indicators.note: rambling suggests wandering about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A convict, upset by a wandering nudist, says that prison would serve the rambler right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One that's offended' reads as a victim, but it is a convict, someone who has committed an offence; 'rambling' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations praising someone's achievement, interchangeable in speech.

clue.text: 'Buck up!' Doctor came offering marsh plant

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: a buck is a male deer

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor who has come tells a patient to cheer up, offering a remedy from a marsh plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DEER into REED; 'Doctor' rearranges CAME into MACE. 'Buck up!' reads as cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the bulrush or cattail, a tall plant of marshes and pond edges.

clue.text: Time's made to meet small Scottish head, showing affected prettiness

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; the 's is a link
wee is Scottish for small
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names

explanation.surface: Time is made to meet a small Scottish chief, who shows off his charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scottish' seems to go with head, but it qualifies small: WEE. A ness is a headland, a head.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for a quality that is twee, cute in a sugary, affected way.

clue.text: Mounting number held up by corrupt hunter pursued by police

indicators.note: held up by in a down clue means sitting on top of the following piece
mounting in a down clue means climbing, so the number word is read upwards
corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rising number of corrupt hunters are being chased by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting' turns NO into ON; 'corrupt' rearranges HUNTER into THERUN; 'held up by' places ON above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chased and evading capture by the law is a common idiom for fugitives.

clue.text: 'Singular creep, supported by Queen,' one writes in haste

indicators.note: supported by in a down clue means resting on the following piece below

parts.note: to crawl is to creep along
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A unique creep, backed by the Queen, writes things down hastily.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who jots untidily and fast is someone writing hurriedly.

clue.text: Satisfied traveller left before Parisian summer

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller
ete is French for summer

explanation.surface: A contented traveller set off before the Paris summer arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: A rep (sales rep) is an old-style commercial traveller; ETE is the French for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being full after eating means being well satisfied, with appetite filled.

clue.text: Entranced by golden eagle?

indicators.note: by means alongside, with the colour placed next

parts.note: rapt means entranced or spellbound
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone is entranced by a golden eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry. 'golden eagle' reads as one bird, but golden is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey; the eagle is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Colour that's successful for a patch but too ornate for a passage

definitions.meaning: a hue between red and blue
a ...-hued patch is a period of success
a florid, over-written passage of prose is described this way

explanation.surface: A colour that works well in a garden patch but is too showy for a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: Patch and passage seem to be places for paint; they complete the phrases for a lucky streak and overwritten prose.
explanation.definitionFit: The hue is also used figuratively for a run of luck and for overblown writing.

clue.text: Pitches needed by terrace for an 11 with bigger members

parts.note: to lob is to pitch or throw high
TER is the abbreviation for terrace in street addresses

explanation.surface: Pitches at a football ground need terraces for a team with larger membership.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a football side; it points to the answer at 11 Across (NIPPERS), here meaning claws, so a creature with bigger claws.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean has much larger pincers than a crab, so it is a claw-bearer with bigger limbs.

clue.text: Wager chap's no expert

parts.note: to lay is to wager or bet
a chap is a man; the 's reads as is, a link

explanation.surface: A man who places a bet is not a professional gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A layperson is a non-specialist, someone without professional knowledge.

clue.text: Carried over Asian island

parts.note: borne means carried
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone was carried across to an island in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring, O stands for an over (six balls).
explanation.definitionFit: A large island of south-east Asia shared by Malaysia, Indonesia and Brunei.

clue.text: Year sitting in weird company making study of fire signs?

indicators.note: sitting in means the year letters are placed inside the scrambled word
weird means strange or out of order, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A strange company of people sitting for a year studying fire signs of the zodiac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges the company letters, and 'sitting in' puts the year inside. Fire signs evokes astrology (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius), but the answer reads omens in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: This is divination by fire, the art of reading omens in flames.

clue.text: Among relics therein lies a cross

indicators.note: therein lies says the answer lies within the letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Among a collection of relics there is a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cross' suggests a religious relic, but it means a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of mixed breed is the product of a cross between types.

clue.text: One featured in Chaucer's tale about first woman

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A character in a Chaucer story concerns Eve, the first woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Canterbury Tales include a tale told by this character, a manor's steward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's pilgrims include a steward who tells his own story in The Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Nun swore to reform grasping daughter and Aussie loafer

indicators.note: grasping means the scrambled letters hold the daughter letter inside
to reform is to remake, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nun vowed to reform a greedy daughter and a lazy Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges NUN SWORE into SUNOWNER; 'grasping' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia the word is slang for a tramp who turns up at sundown, too late to work.
